newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains up on stg, low farm sales, off highs.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains up on stg, low farm sales, off highs.

text.p: LIFFE wheat ended higher on Monday, but off the highs reached earlier in the day.
Prices moved up in early trade on a combination of sterling's losses against the mark since Friday and market surprise that so little grain had come forward off farms after the weekend, traders said.
But the rise got "a little bit overdone", one trader said.
Profit-taking drove prices back down, with shipper selling and merchant price fixing leading the way down,
"The erratic performance on futures is set to continue until we get more on the harvest side," he said.

Active November wheat last traded 1.00 stg higher at 88.50 stg, compared with a high of 89.00 stg, on volume of 205 lots of the total 458. Much of the rest of the volume was on January, which last traded 0.75 stg higher at 90.50 stg on volume of 135 lots. January's high was 91.00 stg.
Barley trade was limited to just 20 lots, 15 of them on September, which last traded 1.00 stg higher at 79.25 stg.
With yields down, farmers have enough storage and so do not feel under pressure to shift grain to clear space "until they want to hold a barn dance", one physical market trader said.
Even so, British cereals farmers did make fast progress with wheat harvesting over the weekend despite showers in some places, analysts said.
"Big strides have been made over the weekend," an expert at the agricultural consultancy ADAS told Reuters.
By last Thursday, some 25 percent of the crop was in and around half was likely to be done by next week, he said.
